newsitem.title: GERMANY: SENTIMENT ON GERMAN DAX STUNG BY LOWER WALL ST.
newsitem.headline: SENTIMENT ON GERMAN DAX STUNG BY LOWER WALL ST.

text.p: German DAX index fell in early bourse trade on Friday, catching up on losses from electronic trade, as a lower close on Wall Street overnight and a touch of pre-weekend catharsis hit sentiment on the stock exchange.
By 0854 GMT the DAX index was down 11.07 points, or 0.25 percent, at 4,403.28 points, while the September DAX future stood at 4,414 points, down 31.
"We've seen some profit-taking initially. Volumes are quieter than they have been, we have got a little bit of stuff on, but this will probably pick up over the day," a trader said.
The Dow Jones Industrial index fell 0.86 percent to 8,188 points overnight, which prompted early jitters among German share traders.

"Wall Street was the initial thing driving the market down. But this is a liquidity-driven market and it doesn't just go away overnight. It's healthy to have a bit of a sell-off, but I think we may yet have a bit of a rally this afternoon," a share trader said.
The focus in early dealings was on financials, particularly the banks as takeover speculation continued with talk of a possible takeover by HSBC of Commerzbank.
Commerzbank was leading volumes and trading ahead against the trend at 65.40 marks, up 1.95 marks or three percent.
Dealers said they did not give the talk much credence, but said the rumours were supporting interest in the bank, long identified as a top takeover candidate.
Deutsche Bank AG was also ahead at 120 marks, up 25 pfennigs.
Dealers expected a sideways trend through the rest of the day, with the continued interest in financials seen preventing any major losses.
